o1.biggest_strength: Eight concrete go/no-go gates (1,000-user beta migration proof, undo, top-200 extension tests, support with engineers on shifts, staged rollout) and a dated timeline that covers all audiences and the freeze.
o1.biggest_mistake: The X post puts several shortcuts and claims in a 5-post thread and the AI builder is shown in launch-day assets, which risks breaking the one-shortcut rule. The table also lists X above Hacker News but ranks by retained users inconsistently (X 3,740 is listed below authors 2,470). Product Hunt is also given its own day, which is fine, but the Show HN is written on launch day. There is also a blank speed placeholder.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Fix the ranking order so it truly follows retained users, add owners to each calendar row, keep one shortcut per message, and trim the five-post thread to something the team can ship tomorrow.

o2.biggest_strength: It opens with a clear decision, ties every move to the 2025 numbers, and gives an owner-assigned calendar that works backward from the freeze, with the author build going out 17 November so bugs are found before 1 December. Measures, plan B and the 10% wave add real management value.
o2.biggest_mistake: Its projection mixes installs and retained users in a confusing way, and the 12-hour reply target is loosely supported. It also gives fewer pre-launch tests with real user numbers than Output 1 and has no beta for power users beyond the authors.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Give a clearer retained-user projection, add a power-user beta for migration proof, and include a short speed number placeholder rule.

reason: Output 2 reads like a plan I can hand to my team tomorrow: owners on every row, a clear decision up front, targets and a plan B, and a tight X post and email in our voice with one shortcut and author credit. Output 1 has stronger migration gates but is busier and has loose ends.
